llamaindex_http_pdf:sequential.summed_process_rss_note: peak of a SUM of per-process RSS (collector.py:360,378). Shared copy-on-write pages are counted once per mapping process, so with N forked workers this OVER-counts by roughly the sharing factor. NOT comparable to Leela's or Shashi's figures.
llamaindex_http_pdf:sequential.comparable_note: Leela reads cgroup memory.stat anon (cgroup_sampler.py:55-62); Shashi reads the Docker API memory_stats.stats.rss, else usage-file (cstats.py:132-140). Both are cgroup-level: the kernel charges a shared page once per cgroup, not once per process. Quote anon against theirs.

cgroup_sampling.anon_mb: point sample taken at end of this leg — NOT a peak
cgroup_sampling.current_mb: point sample taken at end of this leg — NOT a peak
cgroup_sampling.peak_mb: kernel high-water mark, unsampled, cumulative since container start or last reset — spans ALL legs, not just this one

llamaindex_http_pdf:sequential.sharing_factor_note: valid for the sequential leg only (26 processes at peak). Do not apply it to another leg's summed RSS — the over-count scales with the number of processes sharing pages.

rocketride_pdf:sequential.summed_process_rss_note: peak of a SUM of per-process RSS (collector.py:360,378). Shared copy-on-write pages are counted once per mapping process, so with N forked workers this OVER-counts by roughly the sharing factor. NOT comparable to Leela's or Shashi's figures.
rocketride_pdf:sequential.comparable_note: Leela reads cgroup memory.stat anon (cgroup_sampler.py:55-62); Shashi reads the Docker API memory_stats.stats.rss, else usage-file (cstats.py:132-140).
